broadcast.desc: Multicast delegate notifies all listeners. Audio manager, UI, gameplay systems all subscribe. No direct dependencies—each system is separate.
broadcast.label: Event Broadcast

interval.desc: Only refreshes enemy list every N seconds, not every frame. GetAllActorsOfClass is expensive - caching prevents performance hits.
interval.label: Cache Refresh

normalize.desc: Converts raw distance to 0-100% range. Inverted: closer enemy = higher value. Audio systems work with normalized values, not world units.
normalize.label: Normalize Distance

threshold.desc: Only broadcasts when proximity changes significantly. Prevents audio system spam from micro-movements. Typically 1-5% threshold.
threshold.label: Change Threshold

cleanup.desc: Clears timer immediately when movement stops. No lingering footsteps after player halts. Clean state management.
cleanup.label: Timer Cleanup

physmat.desc: Critical flag: bReturnPhysicalMaterial must be true. Without it, PhysMaterial is always null - common Unreal audio gotcha.
physmat.label: Physical Material

timer.desc: Only starts footstep timer when actually moving. Prevents phantom footsteps when standing still. Timer auto-repeats at configured interval.
timer.label: Smart Timer

trace.desc: Shoots ray downward to detect floor surface. Uses Visibility channel. Returns surface type for Wwise Switch selection.
trace.label: Line Trace

hysteresis.desc: Start threshold higher than stop threshold. Enemy at 25% triggers audio, but must drop to 15% to stop. Prevents rapid on/off flickering.
hysteresis.label: Hysteresis Gap

postevent.desc: UAkGameplayStatics::PostEvent triggers audio on this actor. 3D positioned, respects attenuation curves set in Wwise project.
postevent.label: Wwise PostEvent

rtpc.desc: Real-Time Parameter Control. Sends proximity value to Wwise continuously. Controls volume, filter, pitch - smooth modulation, no steps.
rtpc.label: RTPC Update

stopthresh.desc: Lower threshold for stopping audio. Creates hysteresis band that smooths transitions. No audio stutter when enemy hovers at boundary.
stopthresh.label: Stop Threshold

project_akantilado_full_desc: I did the sound design for a student animation about two cats chasing a golden orb through a jungle. Built a 5-layer spatial ambience — canopy birds, mid-level rustling, ground water, wind, wildlife. Pulled all foley from libraries and synced everything frame-by-frame. Delivered two final mixes: stereo for the cinema screening, then 5.1 surround.
project_amorak_block1_content: The creature needed to sound massive. I layered four animal recordings — lion, elephant, tiger, hippo — and pitched them down for weight. The hippo texture gave it that high-end rasp.
project_amorak_block2_content: I designed the environment to follow the camera. Dripping water sits close and unsettling. Distant chains hint at something bigger. Binaural panning pins every sound to a specific spot around your head.
project_amorak_block3_content: The creature always wins in the mix. I set up dynamic ducking so the environment drops whenever the monster screams or the character breathes.
project_amorak_full_desc:
90-second horror teaser where I handled all the audio post-production.

The creature had to feel massive, so I layered four animal recordings — lion, elephant, tiger, hippo — and pitched them down. Built a binaural mix in Reaper with Dear VR Pro and IEM Suite. Delivered stereo binaural at 48kHz/24-bit, -16 LUFS. Took about 4 weeks.

Dynamics chain: CLA-76, LA-2A, LA-3A, C6 multiband.
project_audioq_full_desc: A VST3/AU sampler plugin I built in JUCE and C++. You drag in any audio file and process it with granular synthesis, a hand-coded tremolo, TPT zero-delay filters, and a built-in compressor. Every parameter is DAW-automatable. I wrote the tremolo DSP from scratch — per-sample sine LFO for smooth modulation. Open source on GitHub.
project_gradwork_full_desc: My bachelor thesis. I built a Unity game that talks to AI models through a Python server and tested whether they can generate sounds fast enough for real-time gameplay. Tried ElevenLabs, MMAudio, and AudioGen — none were fast enough. The quickest still took over a second. My workaround: cache sounds during loading screens and serve them under 55ms when needed.
project_not_today_darling_full_desc: I was the only audio person on a 4-player shared-screen racer. No room for subtle stereo work — I was fighting for every decibel of headroom and byte of RAM. End result: loud, chaotic racing that never clips and runs smooth.
project_nottoday_block1_content: A side-scrolling 1-4 player racing game. Chaotic, loud, and ridiculous. I handled everything audio: recording, sound design, music selection, and implementation.
project_nottoday_block2_content: I didn't want the engines to sound like looped MP3s, so I built a MetaSounds graph where pitch and rattle intensity change with speed. You can hear the difference when you drive from carpet to tiles — the sound reacts instantly.
project_pause_and_deserve_full_desc:
A solo horror prototype I built in 8 weeks to learn Unreal Engine 5.

Pausing freezes the enemy, but each pause makes it permanently faster. Audio reacts to your hesitation — forest ambience shifts, breathing scales with proximity, a clock ticks during freeze. MetaSounds + Sound Cues, 100% Blueprints.
project_ray_animation_full_desc: Disco-funk score for a DAE graduation film. The original composer dropped out 8 days before the screening, so I wrote the main track and credits music from scratch — brass, slap bass, DJ scratches, Waves J37 tape effects. Synced every hit to Ray's dance choreography. Got a standing ovation at the premiere.
project_richter_full_desc: Sound design for a student earthquake film. No commercial sample libraries allowed — I recorded all foley from scratch with a Zoom H6 and basic gear. Footsteps on wood, concrete, carpet, door sounds, paper handling. Built tension drones in Vital and ReaSynth. Wrote a short orchestral score timed to scene cuts. The hardest part was keeping dialogue intelligible over the earthquake rumble — used EQ automation and sidechain ducking in Reaper.
project_shadow_frames_collab_desc: Collaboration between RITCS (Story), KASK (Music), and Howest DAE (Game Dev).
project_shadow_frames_full_desc:
A horror game where audio is the core mechanic — players hear anomalies before they see them.

I built the audio systems: footstep surface detection, enemy proximity, anomaly audio, and Wwise integration. Working with RITCS (writers) and KASK (composers).
project_transientica_audiolab_full_desc:
A real-time beatbox recognition system — control rhythm games with your voice.

I optimized audio buffers and the ML pipeline to stay under 60ms latency. Python handles audio analysis, Unity handles gameplay, and they talk over UDP/OSC.
project_transientica_block1_content: The system listens to your microphone and classifies sounds in real-time using an SVM trained on 2000+ samples. You record 30 examples of each drum sound, the model trains in seconds, and you play.
project_transientica_block2_content: Built in Unity with a Python/scikit-learn pipeline. Uses spectral analysis and predictive buffering to hit under 45ms latency.
project_unreal_engine_rebuilder_full_des:
A build automation tool for Unreal Engine.

Unreal sometimes corrupts intermediate files and throws linker errors. This tool does a clean factory reset — clears cache, regenerates project files, and recompiles from scratch. Saves hours of manual cleanup.
project_wwise_unreal_fixer_full_desc:
A rescue tool for Wwise-Unreal integration.

When you migrate Wwise projects or pull from Perforce, Unreal often loses asset paths — SoundBanks, Events, actors go silent. This tool fixes all broken references in one click.

block.anomaly_desc: 10 anomaly types, each with its own audio. 3-stage detection driven by RTPC intensity. Directional audio guides the player to each anomaly.
block.dialogue_desc: Player actions play the right sound through Blueprint delegates. Camera shot, zoom — each fires the right Wwise event.
block.enemy_desc: As the enemy gets closer, audio intensifies. Dread layers and stressed breathing stack up, driven by proximity RTPC with hysteresis thresholds.
block.mixer_desc: Switch Containers paired with the RTPC system. The more photos you collect, the more ambient layers kick in.

challenges_list.c1_prob: Sounds would rapidly toggle on/off when the player stood near trigger edges
challenges_list.c1_sol: Added hysteresis with separate start/stop thresholds (Start at 70%, Stop at 60%)
challenges_list.c2_prob: Calculating distance to every enemy each frame was too expensive
challenges_list.c2_sol: Built a caching system that updates the closest enemy reference periodically instead of every frame

achievements.flicker: Added hysteresis thresholds to prevent audio states from flickering on/off
achievements.opt: Cut CPU load by caching enemy distances and switching to event-based updates

audio_systems.footsteps: Physics-based surface detection via raycasting with velocity-based intervals
audio_systems.mixing: Real-time RTPC modulation of breath and heartbeat based on threat level
audio_systems.spatial: 3D audio cues that guide players to hidden anomalies
